Steps to Reproduce:
1. Launch Minecraft Java Edition 1.16.2.
2. Create a new Creative world.
3. Select "More World Options".
4. Set the World Type to "Superflat".
5. In the "Customize" menu, set the preset to `1;minecraft:air;127;decoration`.
6. Click "Done" to save the preset.
7. Click "Done" again to create the world.
8. Observe that the game crashes upon clicking the "Done" button.
Environment: Minecraft Java Edition Versions: 1.16.2, 1.16.3 Release Candidate 1, 1.16.3
Observed Behavior: When attempting to create a superflat world in Minecraft with only air blocks specified in the generation settings, the game crashes upon clicking the "Done" button. This issue arises specifically when the preset is set to "1 minecraft:air;127;decoration." The crash report for version 1.16.2 indicates a java.lang.IllegalStateException with the message "Missing: ResourceKey[minecraft:worldgen/biome / minecraft:127]," suggesting that the game requires a valid biome to proceed with the world generation. The error occurs during a mouseClicked event handler, and the stack trace shows a series of method calls leading up to the crash, including references to the Render thread and affected screen details. The bug has been confirmed by multiple users, indicating that the game fails to handle the absence of a biome in the superflat world generation, resulting in a crash instead of allowing the creation of an empty world.
Expected Behavior: When creating a superflat world with only air, the game should successfully generate the world without crashing upon clicking the "Done" button. Instead of encountering an error related to a missing biome resource, the player should be able to proceed to the world selection screen and enter the newly created superflat world. This behavior should consistently occur in Java Edition 1.16.2 and later versions.
